::: {.why}
An alert with no documented response is an interruption rather than a control, and the runbook is worth writing now because the moment you need it is the moment you cannot think clearly.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Route alerts to somewhere you will see them, with a severity that distinguishes act-now from read-later.
- Write a runbook entry for each monitor: symptom, likely causes in order, diagnostic commands, and the safe action.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Wire the alerting: email or push for the two severities that need it, with a daily digest for the rest. Test each path by triggering it deliberately, since an untested alert path is the standard way a monitor fails silently.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Write the runbook: one page per monitor with the symptom, the likely causes ranked, the exact commands to run to diagnose, and the safe action, which is usually to flatten or to hold rather than to guess. Include the decision rule for when to stop the system entirely.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
Alerts are routed by severity and every one has a runbook entry with ranked causes, diagnostic commands and a safe action, written before the first real incident rather than after it.
:::
